intake.title: 01 · Intake and intelligence question
intake.description: Define the problem before opening twenty tabs and calling it an investigation.

intake-01.title: Define the central question
intake-01.description: Formulate a specific question that can be answered with observable evidence.

intake-02.title: Define the decision to be supported
intake-02.description: Record what the result will be used for and by whom.

intake-03.title: Record known context
intake-03.description: Separate supplied facts, allegations, assumptions and initial information gaps.

intake-04.title: Define urgency and deadline
intake-04.description: Set the timebox and priority before collection begins.

intake-05.title: Define stop conditions
intake-05.description: Establish when the investigation will be sufficiently answered.

intake-06.title: Define deliverable and audience
intake-06.description: For example: analytical note, executive briefing, technical report or verification record.

intake-07.title: Identify the decision owner and stakeholders
intake-07.description: Record who will make the decision, who consumes the product and who can clarify the requirement.

intake-08.title: Decompose the requirement into intelligence questions
intake-08.description: Turn the central question into smaller, verifiable questions that guide collection.

intake-09.title: Define the decision threshold
intake-09.description: Record which findings would materially change the expected decision, priority or action.

scope.title: 02 · Scope, legality and minimization
scope.description: Define what may, should and should not be collected.

scope-01.title: Define time period and geography
scope-01.description: Record the time window, languages, countries or regions that matter.

scope-02.title: Define permitted sources
scope-02.description: List public-source categories and applicable restrictions.

scope-03.title: Confirm authority and legal basis
scope-03.description: Verify mandate, internal rules and applicable legal requirements.

scope-04.title: Apply data minimization
scope-04.description: Collect only what is necessary to answer the question.

scope-05.title: Define data that must not be recorded
scope-05.description: Avoid credentials, secrets and irrelevant or excessive personal information.

scope-06.title: Identify contact or impact risks
scope-06.description: Plan passive collection when interaction is unnecessary or unauthorized.

scope-07.title: Define passive-collection and interaction boundaries
scope-07.description: Document whether contact, authentication, information requests or other interaction is permitted in the case.

scope-08.title: Define classification, retention and sharing
scope-08.description: Establish how case data will be labelled, stored, shared and disposed of.

opsec.title: 03 · OPSEC and collection environment
opsec.description: Protect the case, sources and the analytic process itself.

opsec-01.title: Use a dedicated research environment
opsec-01.description: Separate investigative activity from personal browsing and accounts.

opsec-02.title: Review browser and session exposure
opsec-02.description: Avoid personal authentication, autofill and unnecessary synchronization.

opsec-03.title: Define an archiving strategy
opsec-03.description: Prepare naming conventions, timestamps and a secure location for evidence.

opsec-04.title: Record tools used
opsec-04.description: Document the tool, version or service and relevant limitations.

opsec-05.title: Avoid unnecessary interaction with the subject
opsec-05.description: Do not like, follow, contact or alter the environment unless this is part of an authorized method.

baseline.title: 04 · Baseline: facts, entities and identifiers
baseline.description: Build the starting point without confusing coincidence with identity.

baseline-01.title: Record known entities
baseline-01.description: Use aliases or internal references whenever possible.

baseline-02.title: Record known identifiers
baseline-02.description: Usernames, domains, corporate emails, corporate phone numbers, public IDs or other authorized pivots.

baseline-03.title: Create a variation list
baseline-03.description: Consider spellings, aliases, transliterations, brands, former names and username patterns.

baseline-04.title: Separate fact, allegation and hypothesis
baseline-04.description: Label each type explicitly before starting pivots.

baseline-05.title: Create secondary questions
baseline-05.description: Which missing information would materially change the conclusion?

baseline-06.title: Assign stable IDs to known entities
baseline-06.description: Create stable references for people, organizations, accounts, domains and other objects before correlating them.

baseline-07.title: List initial critical assumptions
baseline-07.description: Make explicit the assumptions that would change the investigation path or conclusion if wrong.

search.title: 06 · Web discovery and search strategy
search.description: Search in layers, record useful queries and do not depend on one engine.

search-01.title: Run exact searches for identifiers
search-01.description: Start with precise combinations and document relevant results.

search-02.title: Search variations and context
search-02.description: Combine aliases, organization, location, date, event or relevant topic.

search-03.title: Search archived versions
search-03.description: Check page or document history when temporal change matters.

search-04.title: Search public documents and files
search-04.description: Look for presentations, PDFs, spreadsheets, press releases or relevant official material.

search-05.title: Record high-value queries
search-05.description: Keep the queries that produced evidence or need to be repeated.

search-06.title: Record relevant negative results
search-06.description: Absence can constrain hypotheses, but it should not be treated as absolute proof.

search-07.title: Diversify search engines and source types
search-07.description: Avoid depending on a single search engine, platform, index or source class.

search-08.title: Check freshness and temporal validity
search-08.description: Confirm whether the information still represents the period relevant to the intelligence requirement.

search-09.title: Record tool and query limitations
search-09.description: Document coverage, freshness, false positives, regional restrictions and other limitations affecting interpretation.

social.title: 07 · Public presence and SOCMINT
social.description: Map presence and consistency without assuming similar accounts belong to the same entity.

social-01.title: Map official or self-declared profiles
social-01.description: Record URL, stable identifier, observation date and confirmation source.

social-02.title: Search candidate or impersonation profiles
social-02.description: Classify as candidate, likely impersonation or confirmed only when sufficient evidence exists.

social-03.title: Compare biography, avatar and links
social-03.description: Treat consistency across attributes as signals, not standalone identification.

social-04.title: Review public posting history
social-04.description: Observe themes, dates, changes and cross-references relevant to the case.

social-05.title: Map publicly observable relationships
social-05.description: Distinguish interaction, declared association and inferred relationship.

social-06.title: Record platform gaps
social-06.description: Absence from one platform does not mean absence of a digital identity.

social-07.title: Record stable platform identifiers
social-07.description: When public and relevant, record stable IDs in addition to usernames that may change.

social-08.title: Build a basic chronology of relevant accounts
social-08.description: Compare creation, first appearances, name changes, bios, links and other observable milestones.

identifiers.title: 08 · Username and identifier pivots
identifiers.description: Use identifiers as pivots, not automatic proof of identity.

ident-01.title: Search username reuse
ident-01.description: Record only relevant and verifiable matches.

ident-02.title: Compare attributes across candidate accounts
ident-02.description: Dates, links, language, topics, images and mutual references can increase or reduce plausibility.

ident-03.title: Search explicit cross-references
ident-03.description: Prioritize links or statements that directly connect two identifiers.

ident-04.title: Record collisions and namesakes
ident-04.description: Document accounts that appear similar but contain conflicting signals.

ident-05.title: Assess identifier collision and commonness
ident-05.description: Consider whether a username, name, domain or other identifier is common enough to create false links.

ident-06.title: Record the pivot chain
ident-06.description: Document why each pivot led to the next so the correlation can be audited and reproduced.

contact.title: 09 · Email and phone exposure
contact.description: Check public exposure proportionately; do not collect credentials.

contact-01.title: Check public references to authorized email addresses
contact-01.description: Record context and source, not merely occurrence.

contact-02.title: Check exposure indicators through legitimate services
contact-02.description: Use permitted notification/query services and record only necessary metadata.

contact-03.title: Do not store discovered passwords or secrets
contact-03.description: Record only that exposure occurred and handle sensitive material according to applicable policy.

contact-04.title: Check public references to authorized phone numbers
contact-04.description: Record origin, date and context without unnecessarily expanding personal data.

contact-05.title: Corroborate association before attribution
contact-05.description: A shared, recycled or third-party-published phone number or email can mislead.

org.title: 10 · Organizations and public records
org.description: Structure corporate facts before inferring relationships or responsibility.

org-01.title: Confirm legal or institutional identity
org-01.description: Legal name, trade name, jurisdiction and official records when available.

org-02.title: Map official presence
org-02.description: Website, institutional profiles, announcements and official channels.

org-03.title: Check relevant historical changes
org-03.description: Legal name, domain, leadership, institutional addresses or other pertinent public facts.

org-04.title: Map declared corporate relationships
org-04.description: Subsidiaries, parent companies, partners or suppliers only when supported by sources.

org-05.title: Review relevant regulatory or court records
org-05.description: Use official public sources and respect the investigation scope.

infra.title: 11 · Domains and public infrastructure
infra.description: For cyber OSINT, record technical observations with timestamps and scope.

infra-01.title: Confirm domain and declared ownership
infra-01.description: Correlate the official website, records and public documentation.

infra-02.title: Record relevant public DNS data
infra-02.description: Document records pertinent to the case with date and source.

infra-03.title: Review certificates and publicly observable subdomains
infra-03.description: Use public data to map infrastructure relationships without inferring control unless corroborated.

infra-04.title: Check public domain history
infra-04.description: Changes in content, resolution or certificates may be temporally relevant.

infra-05.title: Record exposed services only from passive/authorized sources
infra-05.description: Do not turn an OSINT investigation into intrusive scanning.

infra-06.title: Separate co-hosting from common control
infra-06.description: Shared infrastructure does not automatically prove a relationship between entities.

media.title: 12 · Images, video and documents
media.description: Verify origin, context, chronology and apparent integrity.

media-01.title: Preserve the original file or reference when permitted
media-01.description: Record URL, timestamp and acquisition context.

media-02.title: Run reverse image search
media-02.description: Look for earlier appearances and related versions.

media-03.title: Examine available metadata
media-03.description: Treat metadata as a signal that may be missing, altered or incorrect.

media-04.title: Verify visual content and context
media-04.description: Compare scenery, signs, architecture, weather, shadows, language and other relevant elements.

media-05.title: Verify publication chronology
media-05.description: Identify the earliest publication found without assuming it is the absolute origin.

media-06.title: Record verification limitations
media-06.description: Explain what could not be authenticated or attributed.

geo.title: 13 · GEOINT and temporal verification
geo.description: Geolocation and chronolocation require convergence of signals.

geo-01.title: List observable geographic indicators
geo-01.description: Text, landscape, infrastructure, transport, architecture or local references.

geo-02.title: Compare indicators with independent sources
geo-02.description: Seek confirmation through maps, historical imagery or public official sources.

geo-03.title: Check temporal consistency
geo-03.description: Weather, events, times, page versions and other clues should be compatible.

geo-04.title: State the level of precision
geo-04.description: Distinguish country, city, area and specific location; do not overstate evidentiary resolution.

time-01.title: Build a timeline of relevant events
time-01.description: Include source, timestamp, timezone and confidence level when needed.

time-02.title: Normalize dates and timezones
time-02.description: Avoid incorrect conclusions caused by timezone, republication or delayed capture.

time-03.title: Map relationships with an explicit type
time-03.description: For example: declared by, links to, shares infrastructure, interacts with, employs.

time-04.title: Distinguish correlation from causation
time-04.description: Events close in time or in a graph do not prove a causal relationship.

time-05.title: Record contradictory events
time-05.description: Conflicts are useful data; do not hide them to preserve the narrative.

sources.title: 15 · Source evaluation and corroboration
sources.description: A report's quality rarely exceeds the quality of the sources supporting it.

src-01.title: Assess source origin and proximity
src-01.description: Distinguish primary source, derivative source, republication and aggregator.

src-02.title: Assess credibility and limitations
src-02.description: Consider track record, access, interests, possible bias and collection method.

src-03.title: Corroborate important judgments
src-03.description: Seek independent sources or complementary evidence.

src-04.title: Distinguish multiple sources from multiple copies
src-04.description: Five articles copying the same origin still form one information chain.

src-05.title: Record evidence that contradicts the hypothesis

src-06.title: Test source independence
src-06.description: Check whether apparently distinct sources depend on the same post, statement, dataset or origin.

src-07.title: Assess source access and proximity
src-07.description: Consider whether the source had a realistic ability to observe or know the reported information.

src-08.title: Assess incentives and possible bias
src-08.description: Record interests, context and incentives without dismissing a source solely because bias may exist.

src-09.title: Assess information recency
src-09.description: Confirm whether the source and information are timely enough for the decision or temporal reconstruction.

evidence.title: 16 · Evidence preservation and logging
evidence.description: Make collection auditable and reproducible to the extent necessary.

ev-01.title: Record URL/source and timestamp
ev-01.description: Every material item of evidence should point to its origin and observation time.

ev-02.title: Preserve a copy or capture when appropriate
ev-02.description: Use a method proportionate to the case and applicable rules.

ev-03.title: Record capture context
ev-03.description: Explain what was being observed and why it is relevant.

ev-04.title: Generate hashes for relevant files
ev-04.description: When integrity matters, record the hash and method used.

ev-05.title: Maintain a consistent evidence convention
ev-05.description: IDs, filenames, dates and references should be easy to audit.

ev-06.title: Avoid unnecessary replication of sensitive content
ev-06.description: Preserve the minimum necessary and apply appropriate access controls.

ev-07.title: Distinguish original from derivative evidence
ev-07.description: Mark whether the artifact is original, a copy, capture, transcript, translation, republication or transformation.

ev-08.title: Record acquisition method and reproducibility
ev-08.description: Explain how the evidence was found or captured and what another analyst would need to repeat.

analysis.title: 17 · Structured analysis, alternatives and confidence
analysis.description: Turn data into testable judgments, compare hypotheses and seek what contradicts your reading.

an-01.title: List key judgments
an-01.description: Write the main conclusions as specific, testable statements.

an-02.title: Link each judgment to evidence
an-02.description: No material conclusion should float without a source or explicit reasoning.

an-03.title: Separate observation from inference
an-03.description: Use language that makes clear what was observed and what was interpreted.

an-04.title: Consider alternative hypotheses
an-04.description: Explain at least one plausible alternative when material uncertainty exists.

an-05.title: Assign confidence to judgments
an-05.description: Low, moderate or high, accompanied by the reason and limitations.

an-06.title: Review biases and assumptions
an-06.description: Check confirmation bias, availability, anchoring and overly coherent narratives.

an-07.title: Identify intelligence gaps
an-07.description: List unanswered questions that still matter to the decision.

an-08.title: Run a key-assumptions check
an-08.description: Test the assumptions supporting major judgments and record the impact if they are wrong.

an-09.title: Compare evidence across competing hypotheses
an-09.description: Organize what supports, contradicts or is neutral to each plausible hypothesis.

an-10.title: Actively seek disconfirming evidence
an-10.description: Conduct deliberate searches for information that weakens the preferred hypothesis.

an-11.title: Define what would change the judgment
an-11.description: List indicators or new evidence that would raise, lower or reverse the current assessment.

an-12.title: Assess decision relevance and implications
an-12.description: Connect findings to the original requirement and explain why they do, or do not, change the decision.

report.title: 19 · Reporting, review and closure
report.description: The final product should be useful, traceable and proportionate to the initial question.

rep-01.title: Write the executive summary / BLUF
rep-01.description: Start with the answer, impact and confidence level.

rep-02.title: Document methodology and scope
rep-02.description: Explain sources, period, limitations and relevant exclusions.

rep-03.title: Present findings with references
rep-03.description: Every material finding should be traceable to evidence.

rep-04.title: State limitations and uncertainty
rep-04.description: Do not bury caveats after forty pages of performative certainty.

rep-05.title: Review language and attribution
rep-05.description: Remove claims stronger than the evidence supports.

rep-06.title: Conduct peer review when possible
rep-06.description: Ask for review of evidence, logic and clarity, not just spelling.

rep-07.title: Record open issues and next steps
rep-07.description: Document gaps, necessary monitoring and recommended actions.

rep-08.title: Apply appropriate retention and disposal
rep-08.description: Keep only what is necessary under applicable policy and obligations.

rep-09.title: Explain change or continuity in judgment
rep-09.description: When prior analysis exists, state what changed, what remained and which new evidence caused the revision.

rep-10.title: Include material supporting and contrary evidence
rep-10.description: Do not present only data supporting the main narrative; surface relevant contradictions.

plan.title: 05 · Collection plan and pivot strategy
plan.description: Turn questions into a prioritized collection sequence before browsing without direction.

plan-01.title: Translate questions into collection requirements
plan-01.description: For each intelligence question, define which observable data could answer it.

plan-02.title: Build a source matrix
plan-02.description: Map each question to relevant primary, secondary, official, technical and historical sources.

plan-03.title: Prioritize by information gain, cost and risk
plan-03.description: Start with sources that can reduce the most uncertainty with the least cost, exposure and time.

plan-04.title: Define pivots and exploration order
plan-04.description: Plan which identifiers may unlock new sources and the sequence in which they will be tested.

plan-05.title: Record initial competing hypotheses
plan-05.description: Maintain more than one plausible explanation when the facts allow alternatives.

plan-06.title: Define indicators that support or weaken hypotheses
plan-06.description: List observable signals that would help distinguish competing hypotheses.

plan-07.title: Plan language, locale and timezone variations
plan-07.description: Include transliterations, local names, date formats and regional context when relevant.

plan-08.title: Define continue, pivot, escalate or stop rules
plan-08.description: Decide in advance when a line will be abandoned, deepened, escalated or closed.

decision.title: 18 · Decision gate and analytic sufficiency
decision.description: Stop collecting by habit and test whether the investigation already supports a defensible decision.

decision-01.title: Explicitly answer each intelligence question
decision-01.description: Associate an answer, even if inconclusive, with every question defined at the start.

decision-02.title: Classify the state of each conclusion
decision-02.description: Distinguish supported, partially supported, unsupported and unresolved.

decision-03.title: Assess whether remaining gaps still change the decision
decision-03.description: Determine which gaps are material and which can remain without blocking use of the product.

decision-04.title: Choose the case's next action
decision-04.description: Decide whether to close, collect more, monitor, request specialist support or escalate.

decision-05.title: Separate findings from recommendations
decision-05.description: Do not present a recommended action as though it were an observed fact or attribution judgment.

decision-06.title: Define reassessment triggers
decision-06.description: Record which new events or indicators would require reopening or revising the assessment.

decision-07.title: Calibrate confidence to quality, quantity and gaps
decision-07.description: Ensure confidence reflects actual support rather than the analyst's personal conviction.

closure.title: 20 · Post-case learning and monitoring
closure.description: Close reproducibly and turn what worked, or failed, into methodological improvement.

closure-01.title: Record lessons learned
closure-01.description: Document which approaches saved time, which failed and why.

closure-02.title: Update source and tool limitations
closure-02.description: Record changes, restrictions, false positives and coverage observed during the case.

closure-03.title: Define monitoring or justify its absence
closure-03.description: If residual risk exists, set triggers and cadence; otherwise record why monitoring adds no value.

closure-04.title: Validate reproducibility of critical artifacts
closure-04.description: Confirm another analyst can understand the origin, path and support for the main findings.

closure-05.title: Apply planned archiving and disposal
closure-05.description: Execute the retention, access and disposal rules defined for the case.

closure-06.title: Review the result against the original question and decision
closure-06.description: Check that the final product answered the problem that justified the investigation rather than merely producing interesting data.
